ownershipRule: Commands depend on the smallest semantic application capability that owns their behavior. SQL, staging, publication, and retry mechanics belong to a registered backend leg, not to command code.
commandResolution: Each pinned command ID inherits the one profile whose roots contain its first path segment. A profile lists more than one capability only when the command family composes them. Conditional profiles must be narrowed when that command becomes a vertical port slice.
haxeBoundary: Authored Haxe owns typed application capabilities and transaction intent. Narrow target adapters own unavoidable host storage mechanics. Legacy Go interfaces and direct SQL are evidence, not the desired Haxe API.

capabilities.noStorage: CLI help, discovery, setup, or local context behavior that opens no Beads store.
capabilities.issueReader: Read and filter issue state without changing it.
capabilities.issueLifecycle: Create, update, claim, transition, rename, or delete issue state.
capabilities.graphRelations: Read or mutate dependency edges and derived graph state.
capabilities.commentsAndLabels: Read or mutate issue comments, labels, and tags.
capabilities.workspaceState: Read or mutate repository-scoped configuration, memory, notes, and workflow metadata.
capabilities.batchPlan: Coordinate more than one semantic operation under an explicit batch policy.
capabilities.versionControl: Inspect or publish Dolt working-set, branch, history, remote, or conflict state.
capabilities.backupAndMigration: Initialize, validate, repair, import, export, back up, restore, or migrate stored state.
capabilities.integrationSync: Exchange issue state with a named external integration.
capabilities.eventsJournal: Read, prune, or serve the ordered mutation journal and provenance state.
capabilities.rawSqlAdmin: Run an explicitly administrative or user-supplied SQL operation.
capabilities.serverRuntime: Own a long-lived storage service, proxy, health, or metrics boundary.
capabilities.externalProcess: Delegate behavior to a child process or external tool.

transactionRequirements.none: No Beads storage session is required.
transactionRequirements.readSession: A consistent read session is sufficient; no mutation commits.
transactionRequirements.singleOperation: One semantic storage operation owns its mutation boundary.
transactionRequirements.requestTransaction: Several semantic operations must commit or roll back as one request.
transactionRequirements.unitOfWorkAttempt: A fresh unit of work owns one complete attempt and may replay only under its declared conflict policy.
transactionRequirements.directSql: The command or administrative capability issues SQL at an explicit boundary.
transactionRequirements.externalProcess: A child process or remote system owns the transaction outcome.
transactionRequirements.conditional: Flags, selected subcommands, or runtime routing choose among the other listed requirements.

backendLegs.callbackPolicy: Setup failures may retry before the callback begins. After callback entry, the callback is invoked at most once and an indeterminate commit is never blindly replayed.
backendLegs.publication: By default, a pinned regular SQL transaction commits, selected dirty tables publish to Dolt history, and a separate ignored-table transaction commits. A later failure is an indeterminate durable outcome. Journal mode pins regular, ignored, and journal rows to one SQL transaction before optional history publication.
backendLegs.journal: Enabled journal rows and the mutations they describe share the regular SQL transaction.
backendLegs.hooks: Tracked hooks run only after the complete transaction succeeds and cannot roll it back.

backendLegs.callbackPolicy: The callback runs once inside one embedded SQL transaction. Callers must not blindly replay an indeterminate history publication.
backendLegs.publication: One SQL transaction commits all table classes, then selected dirty tables publish to Dolt history. A failure after SQL commit is an indeterminate durable outcome.
backendLegs.journal: Journal activation is scoped to the same embedded SQL transaction as the mutation.
backendLegs.hooks: Tracked hooks run only after the complete transaction succeeds and cannot roll it back.

backendLegs.callbackPolicy: Serialization failures can replay the complete callback against a fresh unit of work within a bounded retry budget. Other callback and commit failures are permanent for that run.
backendLegs.publication: Each unit of work owns and commits its attempt. An empty message commits ephemeral SQL state without Dolt history; a non-empty message publishes versioned state.
backendLegs.journal: The provider scopes journal activation to the unit of work's pinned transaction.
backendLegs.hooks: Hook completion remains an after-commit application concern; it is not part of the unit-of-work commit.

batchSemantics.requirement: All requested creates and their creation-time relations use one request transaction when the command promises all-or-nothing behavior.
Validation can reject individual inputs before the surviving close set commits together; the external partial-result policy remains command-owned.
A heterogeneous mutation plan requires one atomic application boundary.

directSqlCensus.policy: Every matching production source is an explicit port obligation. Command-direct matches require semantic reassignment or a narrow raw-SQL justification; no match is automatically approved.

ratifiedLegDifferences: Importer has a semantic UOW accessor; both store legs still use the legacy raw import seam.
Bootstrap history is recorded outside the role on store legs and inside the role on UOW.
UOW has no caller-held working set or separate staging contract because every unit of work commits itself.

gaps.need: Classify all 34 command-direct SQL sources as semantic capability calls or justified administrative SQL boundaries.
Execute pre-callback, callback, SQL commit, history publication, and after-commit hook failures per admitted backend leg.
Preserve the bd sql mutating-query and common-table-expression policy without treating arbitrary text as read-only.
Inventory command and runtime switches that enable journal recording and hook execution.
Record best-effort repair and history publication behavior for doctor operations.
